consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is a God-given new identity, character, and status (personal or corporate) conferred on the redeemed/overcomer, marking transformation, belonging, and eschatological acceptance, based on renaming narratives and Rev/Isa promises.
book_summary: The book defines the new name as the renewed covenant, known and kept only by the one who receives it.
book_core_identification: the renewed covenant (known/kept only by recipient)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus covers cases of personal renaming (Abram/Jacob/Peter), corporate Zion restoration, and overcomer eschatology as identity change; book reassigns the symbol wholly to the renewed covenant as private possession rather than any identity designation.
material_contradiction: Book replaces the consensus referent (transformed identity/character) with a distinct referent (the renewed covenant itself); the two cannot both be the primary identification of the same symbol in the same sense.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus centers on new identity drawn from OT renamings and apocalyptic bestowal, while the book centers on the renewed covenant characterized by exclusive knowledge/keeping (drawing especially from the secrecy clause of Rev 2:17). This substitutes rather than narrows or refines the central referent; no primary or alternative consensus reading equates the new name with the covenant. The book's own common-view note acknowledges and departs from the identity reading.
strongest_objection: The cited renaming texts (Gen 32; Isa 62; 65) and their standard exegesis treat the new name as designating changed status/identity, not as identical to the covenant; covenant language is at best ambient and does not license equating the two.
